evals.prompt: /teach the basics of chess openings — I've never played before and want to actually get better, not just read a summary
evals.expected_output: The agent treats the current directory as a teaching workspace: interviews the user for a concrete mission before writing anything, writes MISSION.md once confirmed, checks/populates RESOURCES.md with real trusted sources, then produces one short self-contained HTML lesson file under lessons/ (numbered 0001-<slug>.html) scoped to a single tightly-scoped opening concept, tied to the mission, citing a primary source, and ending with a prompt to ask follow-up questions.
expectations: The agent asks about the user's underlying goal (why chess openings, what 'better' looks like) before drafting a lesson, rather than jumping straight to content
MISSION.md is created following the Why / Success looks like / Constraints / Out of scope structure and is confirmed with the user
RESOURCES.md is created or checked before the lesson is written, with at least one annotated, high-trust source

Exactly one lesson is produced as a single self-contained HTML file in lessons/, named with the 0001-<slug>.html numbering convention, scoped to one tightly-scoped idea rather than all of chess openings at once
The lesson links to a primary source and includes a reminder that the user can ask follow-up questions
No glossary term or learning record is added purely on exposure — only if the user demonstrates understanding during the exchange
